headline: Data Center Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill requires large energy users, such as data centers, to pay for the costs of increasing electric generating capacity, preventing these costs from being passed on to residential customers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Governor Abigail Spanberger's administration, Senator L. Louise Lucas, Del. Destiny LeVere Bolling, consumer advocacy groups, residential ratepayers.
opponents: Data center industry, Dominion Energy (initially, due to amendments).
news_headline: Virginia Shifts Data Center Energy Costs to High-Demand Users
news_summary: New legislation in Virginia mandates that data centers and other large energy users consuming 25 MW or more must bear the costs of increased electric generating capacity, preventing these expenses from being passed to residential customers. Senator L. Louise Lucas, the bill sponsor, advocated for data centers to "pay their fair share" as residents' energy costs climb.

headline: Data Center Water Consumption Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water utilities providing water to data centers to report monthly water consumption to the State Water Control Board, increasing transparency on water usage.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Senator Kannan Srinivasan, environmental groups, local governments, water conservation advocates.
opponents: Data center industry (potentially, due to increased reporting burden).
news_headline: Virginia Bill Addresses Data Center Water Use Transparency
news_summary: SB 553 addresses water use transparency by requiring utilities to report how much water data centers consume. This aims to give communities clearer insight into local resource use, as such data has often been kept private.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities, requiring site assessments for sound profiles near residential areas and schools, and allowing localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic resources.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Del. Joshua Thomas, Senator Danica Roem, local residents, community advocates, environmental groups, local governments.
opponents: Data center industry, developers (potentially, due to increased regulatory burden).
news_headline: New Siting Requirements for Virginia Data Centers
news_summary: HB 153 introduces new siting requirements for large data centers, mandating impact assessments on agriculture, parks, and historical sites before rezoning approval. Lawmakers see this as a foundation for stronger future regulations on where data centers can be built and how they affect surrounding communities.
